title: Rapid, Large-Scale and Multi-Species Phylogenomic Analysis of Orthoebolaviruses Using Covary
content: Orthoebolaviruses are important viral pathogens that continue to cause outbreaks with significant public health consequences. As genomic surveillance efforts expand, there is an increasing need for rapid and scalable approaches for large-scale viral genome analysis. This study evaluated Covary, a translation-aware and alignment-free computational framework, for the phylogenomic analysis of complete Orthoebolavirus genomes. A total of 728 complete genomes representing six Orthoebolavirus species and Orthomarburgvirus marburgense were analyzed using Covary. Translation-aware genomic embeddings were generated and examined using pairwise distance analysis, t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE), hierarchical clustering, and pairwise distance heatmaps to assess genome-wide and species-level relationships. Most analyzed taxa formed distinct and taxonomically consistent clusters, demonstrating that Covary preserved biologically meaningful genome-wide relationships despite operating without multiple sequence alignment. Quantitative analysis of the embedding-derived distance matrix further demonstrated a consistent genome-wide distance structure across the dataset, supporting the robustness of the recovered relationships. Reston, Sudan, Bundibugyo, and Taï Forest ebolaviruses, together with Marburgvirus, exhibited clear species-level organization. In contrast, Orthoebolavirus zairense genomes were dispersed across multiple regions of the embedding space, indicating greater genome-wide diversity relative to the other analyzed species. The expected species-level clustering observed following the exclusion of O. zairense genomes suggests that the observed dispersion reflects biological characteristics of the species rather than limitations of the analytical framework. These findings demonstrate that translation-aware embeddings can effectively recover species-level relationships while providing additional insight into genome-wide diversity among Orthoebolavirus species. Overall, Covary provides a rapid, scalable, and biologically informative framework for comparative whole-genome analysis, with potential applications in comparative genomics, genomic surveillance, and the study of viral evolution.
